name: Cheerleaders
description: A non-pawn piece may capture only while adjacent to one of the affected player's pawns.
ambiguities: Adjacency is measured before the move and includes diagonal adjacency.

name: Noble Steed
description: A non-knight piece may move only while adjacent to one of the affected player's knights.
ambiguities: The knight exception applies to the primary mover; castling tests the king origin.

name: Pack Mentality
description: A piece must finish adjacent to another one of the affected player's pieces.
ambiguities: Castling is permitted because its resulting king and rook are adjacent.

name: Separation Anxiety
description: A pawn that starts adjacent to its king may not leave the king's adjacent squares.
ambiguities: The king may leave an adjacent pawn behind, matching the observed parenthetical clarification.

name: Separation of Church and State
description: Bishops cannot move adjacent to a king, and kings cannot move adjacent to a bishop.
ambiguities: Both kings and bishops of either color count; a captured bishop is removed before king adjacency is assessed.

name: Sibling Rivalry
description: A piece cannot finish adjacent to an opposing piece of the same resulting type.
ambiguities: Promotion uses the promoted type; en-passant removes its victim before adjacency is evaluated; castling evaluates both king and rook.

name: Social Distancing
description: A non-capturing move cannot finish adjacent to an opposing piece.
ambiguities: En-passant is a capture and is exempt. Castling is evaluated by the logged king destination; the secondary rook destination is not a separate candidate move.

name: Spread Out
description: A non-pawn piece cannot finish adjacent to another own non-pawn piece, and castling is forbidden.
ambiguities: A promotion remains a pawn move for this restriction.

name: Torchlight
description: A non-pawn move must start or finish adjacent to one of the affected player's pawns.
ambiguities: The pre-move pawn placement lights both origin and destination squares. Castling is evaluated as the logged king move rather than a second rook move.

name: Royal Berth
description: A move cannot place one of the affected player's pieces adjacent to their king.
ambiguities: King moves are checked against every other own piece in the resulting position; castling is forbidden because it places the rook adjacent.

name: Peons First
description: A piece cannot move while directly one square behind one of the affected player's pawns.
ambiguities: Behind is color-relative and requires the same file. Castling tests the logged king origin; the secondary rook is not treated as a separate candidate mover.

name: Power Cells
description: A move's Manhattan distance cannot exceed the affected player's current pawn count.
ambiguities: With no pawns, no ordinary move has distance zero, so the player loses for having no drawback-legal move.

name: Leading the Charge
description: While a knight remains, non-knights cannot move ahead of the most advanced own knight.
ambiguities: Ahead is color-relative by destination rank; knights themselves are unrestricted.

name: Scouting Ahead
description: While a pawn remains, non-pawns cannot move ahead of the most advanced own pawn.
ambiguities: Ahead is color-relative by destination rank; pawn moves including promotions are unrestricted.

name: Diplomatic Immunity
description: A piece that just made a non-capturing move cannot be captured immediately.
ambiguities: Both physical pieces moved by castling receive immunity; en-passant identifies the captured pawn square rather than the capturing destination.

name: Flatterer
description: The affected player must match whether the opponent's previous mover was a pawn or non-pawn.
ambiguities: Promotion is classified by its primary pawn mover; castling is a non-pawn move.

name: Hipster
description: The affected player cannot move the same primary piece type as the opponent's previous mover.
ambiguities: Promotion is classified as a pawn move and castling as a king move.

name: Hedonic Treadmill
description: The resulting piece must be at least as valuable as the opponent's previously moved resulting piece.
ambiguities: A promotion is valued as its resulting promoted type; kings have effectively infinite value.

name: Ladies First
description: The king may move only when the affected player's previous primary mover was the queen.
ambiguities: A pawn promotion to queen does not authorize the next king move.

name: Centralized Command
description: A capture is permitted only if the affected player moved their king within their previous three turns.
ambiguities: The window counts three affected-player turns rather than three plies; castling counts as a king move.

name: Royal Jubilee
description: After capturing a non-pawn piece, the affected player's next mover must be a king or queen.
ambiguities: Promotion to queen remains a pawn move and cannot satisfy the response.

name: Monkey See
description: The affected player may capture only with piece types the opponent has previously captured with.
ambiguities: Capture types accumulate permanently and use the primary mover type.

name: Haunted
description: The affected player cannot move to a square where they previously made a capture.
ambiguities: For en-passant, the logged landing square becomes haunted.

name: Scorched Earth
description: The affected player cannot move to a square they previously moved from.
ambiguities: Castling burns both the king and rook origin squares.

name: Turn the Other Cheek
description: The affected player cannot immediately recapture.
ambiguities: Recapture means capturing onto the immediately preceding opponent capture destination.

name: Velociraptor
description: A captured piece type must have been a primary mover for the opponent within their previous three turns.
ambiguities: The window counts opponent turns and uses primary mover types for promotion and castling.

name: Windup Toys
description: From standard move thirteen onward, knights and bishops cannot move.
ambiguities: The first twelve fullmove numbers are unrestricted; the restriction begins at FEN fullmove 13 for both colors.

name: Doctor Octopus
description: The affected player may make at most eight captures of non-king pieces.
ambiguities: Exactly eight non-king captures are allowed; standard legal chess never captures a king.

name: Cowering in Fear
description: A mover cannot be less valuable than the most valuable piece the opponent has captured.
ambiguities: The highest historical captured value is the threshold; promotion is valued by the pre-move pawn identity; kings have effectively infinite value.

name: Crenellations
description: Pawns may move only to squares of one hidden color.
ambiguities: The hidden color is fixed for the game; promotion is still a pawn move and uses its destination color.

name: Theocracy
description: On hidden odd- or even-numbered moves, captures may only be made by bishops.
ambiguities: Move number means the standard FEN fullmove number; quiet moves remain legal on the active parity.

name: Active Volcano
description: No piece may land on or orthogonally adjacent to one hidden square.
ambiguities: The square is fixed for the game; sliders may pass over affected squares because only destinations are forbidden. The eight-square c4-f5 parameter domain is inferred from all available observations and remains unverified. Castling is evaluated by the logged king destination, not the secondary rook destination.

name: Comfort Zone
description: If any ordinary legal move reaches one hidden square, the affected player must choose one.
ambiguities: The destination is fixed for the game; when no ordinary legal move reaches it, the rule provides no evidence and all ordinary moves remain legal. The eight-square c4-f5 parameter domain is inferred from all available observations and remains unverified. Castling is evaluated by the logged king destination, not the secondary rook destination.
